locator: VII, lect. 2 nn. 894-896: a halt must be made
interpretation: With the added assumption that mover and moved touch or are continuous, so that the infinite series forms one magnitude, an infinite motion in finite time follows, which is impossible; the assumption is contingent for movers and mobiles in general, and an impossibility does not follow from a contingent premise, so the series does not go on to infinity and 'there will exist a first mobile which is being moved by a mover that is immovable'. Read as the same proposition as Aristotle's claim ARIST-PHYS-242B23-SERIES-HAS-FIRST-A. The bodily-continuity proof is Aristotle's Physics VII argument, not the per se ordering argument of ST I q.2 a.3. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
